name: Japanese Mission Focus Subset v1
description: Relationship-first active subset for the next build and early study.

notes.usage_note: Use with anyone you don't know well. With close friends, おはよう alone is fine.
notes.example_japanese: おはようございます！今日も よい一日を。
notes.literal_breakdown: Good morning! Today also → good day [have].
notes.example_english: Good morning! Have a great day today too.
notes.source_front_text:
おはようございます

(ohayou gozaimasu)
notes.source_back_text:
おはようございます

(ohayou gozaimasu)

Good morning (polite)

Use with anyone you don't know well. With close friends, おはよう alone is fine.

おはようございます！今日も　よい一日を。

📐 Good morning! Today also → good day [have].

Good morning! Have a great day today too.

notes.usage_note: The standard daytime greeting. Safe to use with absolutely anyone.
notes.example_japanese: こんにちは！はじめまして。
notes.source_front_text:
こんにちは

(konnichiwa)
notes.source_back_text:
こんにちは

(konnichiwa)

Hello / Good afternoon

The standard daytime greeting. Safe to use with absolutely anyone.

こんにちは！はじめまして。

📐 Hello! → First time meeting.

Hello! Nice to meet you.

notes.usage_note: Used after the sun goes down. Same politeness as こんにちは.
notes.example_japanese: こんばんは！礼拝は どうでしたか？
notes.example_english: Good evening! How was the service?
notes.source_front_text:
こんばんは

(konbanwa)
notes.source_back_text:
こんばんは

(konbanwa)

Good evening

Used after the sun goes down. Same politeness as こんにちは.

こんばんは！礼拝は　どうでしたか？

📐 Good evening! Service [topic] → how was?

Good evening! How was the service?

notes.usage_note: Said when someone is going to sleep or leaving for the night. Not a general goodbye.
notes.example_japanese: おやすみなさい。また明日！
notes.source_front_text:
おやすみなさい

(oyasumi nasai)
notes.source_back_text:
おやすみなさい

(oyasumi nasai)

Good night

Said when someone is going to sleep or leaving for the night. Not a general goodbye.

おやすみなさい。また明日！

📐 Good night. Again tomorrow!

Good night. See you tomorrow!

notes.usage_note: Carries a sense of finality — like you won't see them for a long time. Use またね for casual.
notes.example_japanese: さようなら。また来年 会いましょう。
notes.literal_breakdown: Goodbye. Again next year → let's meet.
notes.example_english: Goodbye. Let's meet again next year.
notes.source_front_text:
さようなら

(sayounara)
notes.source_back_text:
さようなら

(sayounara)

Goodbye (formal / final)

Carries a sense of finality — like you won't see them for a long time. Use またね for casual.

さようなら。また来年　会いましょう。

📐 Goodbye. Again next year → let's meet.

Goodbye. Let's meet again next year.

notes.usage_note: Casual goodbye used with people you know.
notes.example_japanese: じゃあね！連絡してね。
notes.source_front_text:
じゃあね / またね

(jaa ne / mata ne)
notes.source_back_text:
じゃあね / またね

(jaa ne / mata ne)

See you / Bye (casual)

Friendly warm goodbye. Use with people you've gotten to know on the trip.

じゃあね！連絡してね。

📐 Bye! Contact [please do], okay?

Bye! Stay in touch.

notes.english: See you later / bye for now
notes.usage_note: Friendly warm goodbye; better than さようなら for casual follow-up.

notes.english: Nice to meet you (first meeting only)
notes.usage_note: ONLY for the very first time you meet someone. Always follow with よろしくお願いします.
notes.example_japanese: はじめまして。ジョンです。よろしく！
notes.literal_breakdown: First meeting. Jon → am. Please treat me well!
notes.example_english: Nice to meet you. I'm Jon. Pleased to meet you!

はじめまして

(hajimemashite)
notes.source_back_text:

(hajimemashite)

📐 First meeting. Jon → am. Please treat me well!

Nice to meet you. I'm Jon. Pleased to meet you!

notes.english: Pleased to meet you / Please be kind to me
notes.usage_note: No perfect English translation. Closes a self-intro and expresses goodwill. Never skip it!

notes.literal_breakdown: America [from] came. → Kindly please treat me.

notes.usage_note: The full polite thank you. Use with anyone you want to show respect.
notes.example_japanese: 助けてくれて ありがとうございます。

ありがとうございます

(arigatou gozaimasu)
notes.source_back_text:
ありがとうございます

(arigatou gozaimasu)

Thank you (polite)

The full polite thank you. Use with anyone you want to show respect.

助けてくれて　ありがとうございます。

📐 Help [giving me] → thank you.

Thank you for helping me.
notes.japanese: ありがとうございます

notes.usage_note: Formal response to ありがとう. In casual settings, 大丈夫 or いいえ also work.
notes.example_japanese: ありがとう！— どういたしまして。

(douitashimashite)
notes.source_back_text:

notes.usage_note: Gets someone's attention OR lightly apologizes. One of the most-used words on any Japan trip!
notes.example_japanese: すみません、トイレは どこですか？
notes.example_english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
notes.source_front_text:
すみません

(sumimasen)
notes.source_back_text:
すみません

(sumimasen)

Excuse me / I'm sorry

Gets someone's attention OR lightly apologizes. One of the most-used words on any Japan trip!

すみません、トイレは　どこですか？

📐 Excuse me, restroom [topic] → where is?

Excuse me, where is the restroom?

notes.usage_note: Stronger than すみません. Use when you've actually done something wrong.
notes.example_japanese: 遅れて ごめんなさい。
notes.source_front_text:
ごめんなさい

(gomen nasai)
notes.source_back_text:
ごめんなさい

(gomen nasai)

I'm sorry (genuine apology)

Stronger than すみません. Use when you've actually done something wrong.

遅れて　ごめんなさい。

📐 Being late [for] → I'm sorry.

I'm sorry for being late.

notes.english: It's okay / I'm fine / No problem
notes.usage_note: Very versatile. Can mean 'I'm fine,' 'no worries,' or even 'no thank you' depending on context.
notes.example_japanese: 大丈夫ですか？— はい、大丈夫です。
notes.literal_breakdown: Okay are you? → Yes, okay am.
notes.example_english: Are you okay? — Yes, I'm fine.
notes.source_front_text:
大丈夫です

(daijoubu desu)
notes.source_back_text:
大丈夫です

(daijoubu desu)

It's okay / I'm fine / No problem

Very versatile. Can mean 'I'm fine,' 'no worries,' or even 'no thank you' depending on context.

大丈夫ですか？— はい、大丈夫です。

📐 Okay are you? → Yes, okay am.

Are you okay? — Yes, I'm fine.

notes.usage_note: Polite yes.
notes.example_japanese: 教会に来ますか？— はい、行きます。
notes.example_english: Will you come to church? — Yes, I will.
notes.source_front_text:
はい / いいえ

(hai / iie)
notes.source_back_text:
はい / いいえ

(hai / iie)

Yes / No

はい is polite yes. いいえ is no. In casual speech, うん (yes) and ううん (no) are used.

教会に来ますか？— はい、行きます。

📐 Church to come? → Yes, go.

Will you come to church? — Yes, I will.

notes.usage_note: Polite no.
notes.example_japanese: 教会に来ますか？— はい、行きます。

📐 Church to come? → Yes, go.

Will you come to church? — Yes, I will.

notes.usage_note: わかります = I understand. わかりません = I don't understand. You'll use both constantly.
notes.example_japanese: 少し わかります。でも、ゆっくり 話してください。
notes.literal_breakdown: A little → understand. But, slowly → please speak.
notes.example_english: I understand a little. But please speak slowly.
notes.source_front_text:
わかります

(wakarimasu)
notes.source_back_text:
わかります

(wakarimasu)

I understand

📐 A little → understand. But, slowly → please speak.

I understand a little. But please speak slowly.

notes.usage_note: Literally 'one more time, please.' Never be embarrassed to use this — people will appreciate it.
notes.example_japanese: すみません、もう一度 お願いします。
notes.literal_breakdown: Excuse me, one more time → please.

(mou ichido onegaishimasu)
notes.source_back_text:

(mou ichido onegaishimasu)

📐 Excuse me, one more time → please.

Excuse me, please say that again.

notes.usage_note: 少し = a little. Humble and honest. Sets good expectations and earns instant goodwill.

notes.usage_note: お元気 = your wellbeing (お makes it polite). A warm, caring way to greet someone.

notes.usage_note: One of the most natural filler phrases in Japanese. Shows you're listening and agreeing.

notes.english: I see / Makes sense / Ah, I understand

(naruhodo)

このバスは　札幌駅に　行きます。— なるほど！

📐 This bus [topic] → Sapporo station [to] → goes. — I see!

This bus goes to Sapporo Station. — Ah, I see!

notes.usage_note: また = again. 会いましょう = let's meet. Warm and genuine — perfect for ending a good conversation.

📐 Again → let's meet. Contact → please do.

Let's meet again. Please keep in touch.
